names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 25 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Αννιανός Επίσκοπος Αλεξανδρείας», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 25. април ст. ст., „Св. Аниан, други епископ Александријски.“ Св. is not a rank, and the appositive clause after the comma — други епископ Александријски, the second bishop of Alexandria — is the grade and the see, which this folder keeps in `types` and in `office` and which `honorific.js` composes back. The heading gives no epithet, so the bare forename is the whole of the Serbian form.

death.note: saint.gr prints three readings and settles none: «Κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το έτος 82 μ.Χ. Κατά άλλη μαρτυρία τελεύτησε κατά την εποχή του αυτοκράτορα Δομετιανού, δηλαδή το έτος 85 μ.Χ. Άλλη όμως παράδοση Ανατολικής προελεύσεως αναφέρει ότι ποίμανε την Εκκλησία της Αλεξάνδρειας επί δέκα οκτώ έτη και κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το έτος 86 μ.Χ.» — so the interval carries all three.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 25ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Αννιανός Επίσκοπος Αλεξανδρείας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 25 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page makes him the disciple of Mark the Evangelist and his successor on the episcopal throne of Alexandria, quotes Eusebius of Caesarea calling him «ανήρ θεοφιλής και κατά πάντα θαυμάσιος», and tells the meeting: a cobbler at Alexandria while still a pagan, he wounded his own left hand with his tool while mending Mark's broken shoes, and Mark asked him to believe in God in order to be healed, made clay from his spittle, anointed the hand and called on the Name of the Lord, and the hand was made well; after which Annianus was baptized by Mark and succeeded him. **It prints three years for his death and settles none of them**, 82, or 85 under Domitian, or 86 after eighteen years of shepherding the Church of Alexandria, so the interval here carries all three. Under «Ιερά Λείψανα» it puts his relics in the Roman Catholic church of St Thomas at Venice. It prints no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 08.05.2026 (25. април ст. ст.) — „Св. Аниан, други епископ Александријски.“

attestations.note: The heading names him the second bishop of Alexandria and the entry is the same meeting saint.gr tells — the cobbler who wounded his own left hand mending Mark's shoe, the healing with spittle, the baptism, the succession — so this is that man and not a second folder. **It gives no year**, so the three readings this folder already carries for his death, 82, 85 or 86, were left exactly as they stood and nothing was narrowed. New from this book: that Mark's shoe split on one foot as he stepped from the ship onto dry land; that the tool was **шило**, an awl, driven through the left hand, and that the cobbler cried out with the pain; that Mark mixed **прашину с пљувачком**, dust with his own spittle, rather than clay; that the cobbler marvelled and asked Mark home; that **he was baptized with his whole household**; and that it was the devoutness and the zeal he then showed in the work of God for which Mark ordained him bishop. The Prologue prints no hymn of any kind.
